prompt.context_jp: いつもと変わらぬ挨拶が交わされるが、悦子の声___どこか沈んでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: いつもと変わらぬ挨拶が交わされるが、悦子の声___どこか沈んでいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the contrastive 'but her voice was somehow heavy' nuance.

feedback.correct_en: は contrasts Etsuko's voice against the ordinary greetings — the greetings are normal, but her voice (as for her voice) is heavy.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the voice as brand-new information, losing the contrast with the preceding clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 料理はおいしいが、店の雰囲気はいまいちだ。
contrast_examples.en: The food is good, but the atmosphere isn't great.
Suddenly a voice came out (new info).

prompt.context_jp: 出勤前の慌ただしい支度の中、森尾登代子のスマートフォン___小さく震えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 森尾登代子のスマートフォン___小さく震えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for this new-event sentence.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the phone vibrating as a new event entering the scene — a sudden occurrence the narrator reports.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the phone as an already-established topic, which doesn't match this scene-introducing event.

contrast_examples.jp: そのドアはいつも開いている。

prompt.context_jp: カウンターの奥に座る今井セシル___、頬杖をついてぼんやりとエントランスを眺めている。
prompt.prompt_jp: カウンターの奥に座る今井セシル___、頬杖をついてぼんやりとエントランスを眺めている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets Cecil as the paragraph topic.

feedback.correct_en: は establishes Cecil as the topic the paragraph will describe — multiple predicates (propping chin, gazing) hang off her as theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report her presence as new info, which clashes with the extended description that follows.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は窓際に座り、本を読んでいる。
contrast_examples.en: She sits by the window and is reading.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰かが窓際に座っている。
contrast_examples.en: Someone is sitting by the window.

prompt.context_jp: そこを通りかかった悦子___、ふいに柱の陰で足を止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこを通りかかった悦子___、ふいに柱の陰で足を止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for Etsuko appearing on scene.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces Etsuko into the scene as a new participant — 'Etsuko, who happened to pass by, suddenly stopped.' It's an event/arrival report.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presume Etsuko is already the established topic, but here she's just entering the lobby scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 知らない人が声をかけてきた。
contrast_examples.en: A stranger spoke to me (new entrant).
That person is my senior (known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 気になったことは確認しないと気が済まないから、それ___校閲の仕事だと思うし 私のやり方だから
prompt.prompt_jp: それ___校閲の仕事だと思うし 私のやり方だから
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'THAT is the proofreader's job.'

feedback.correct_en: は treats それ as topic — 'as for that (the checking), it's the proofreader's job.' She's explaining what that behavior is.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively single out 'it is THAT (and nothing else) that is the job,' which is not her nuance here.

contrast_examples.en: THAT is my job (singling it out).

prompt.context_jp: 足を投げ出した悦子の頬___、疲労と満足で赤らんでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 足を投げ出した悦子の頬___、疲労と満足で赤らんでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle describing her cheeks as the known topic.

feedback.correct_en: は takes 'Etsuko's cheeks' as topic — the sentence then describes their state (flushed). A typical descriptive sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the cheeks as newly introduced, but we are continuing to describe known Etsuko.

prompt.context_jp: 団子をほおばる悦子の鞄の底で、携帯電話___短く震えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 携帯電話___短く震えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the phone ringing as a sudden event.

feedback.correct_en: が reports the phone vibrating as a sudden new event in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the phone a pre-established topic, which doesn't fit this surprise occurrence.

prompt.context_jp: 森尾___仕事のことで ちょっと落ち込んでてね
prompt.prompt_jp: 森尾___仕事のことで ちょっと落ち込んでてね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing Morio's situation as new info to Kaizuka.

feedback.correct_en: Etsuko is reporting new background info to Kaizuka ('Morio was feeling down about work'). が marks this subordinate-clause-like new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'Morio' the topic of a general statement; here she's explaining a specific recent situation.

contrast_examples.en: My kid got a fever, you see…

prompt.context_jp: ゲラの文字を追う森尾の指___、ふいに止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ゲラの文字を追う森尾の指___、ふいに止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Morio's fingers suddenly stopping.

feedback.correct_en: が marks a sudden event observed by the narrator — the fingers stopping is a noteworthy new happening.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the fingers as an ongoing topic, undermining the sense of sudden pause.

prompt.context_jp: 登紀子の眉___、ほんの少しだけ上がった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 登紀子の眉___、ほんの少しだけ上がった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the eyebrow movement.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the subtle movement as an observed event — a telling physical reaction the narrator points out.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'her eyebrows' a general topic, losing the punch of the momentary reaction.

prompt.context_jp: (前:無駄な作業と言われても致し方ありません。) ですが… これ___我々 校閲の仕事です
prompt.prompt_jp: これ___我々 校閲の仕事です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'but THIS is our job.'

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes これ against the preceding 'useless' claim — 'as for this, it is our job.' A classic contrastive-は statement of identity.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively specify 'THIS (alone) is the job,' not matching the explanatory tone.

prompt.context_jp: ちょうどそのとき、校閲部の電話___次々と鳴り始めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 校閲部の電話___次々と鳴り始めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for a scene-opening event.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the phones ringing as a sudden new event that drives the scene forward.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the phones the topic of a general statement, losing the 'just then' immediacy.

prompt.context_jp: 「大将___さぁ 仕事 楽しい？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「大将___さぁ 仕事 楽しい？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'Master, is your work fun?'

feedback.correct_en: は sets 'Master' as the topic she's asking about — a general question about his experience. The さぁ softens the topic marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively single him out ('it's the Master whose job is fun'), which doesn't fit a casual question.

contrast_examples.en: Is Dad doing okay? (asking about topic)
Who is doing well? (exhaustive answer with が)

prompt.context_jp: (森尾、幸人に:) 「好き___なんだ 先輩のこと」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「好き___なんだ 先輩のこと」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this confession-like statement.

feedback.correct_en: With adjectives like 好きだ, the thing liked is marked with が. Here 先輩のこと is the (postposed) が-marked object: '(I) like senpai.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would strongly contrast ('as for senpai, I like her') and sounds odd for a direct confession.

prompt.context_jp: いや あの日のデート ドタキャンすることになっちゃって 本当 ごめんねって 言おうと思って来たのに 逆に___ 言われちゃうとはな
prompt.prompt_jp: 逆に___ 言われちゃうとはな
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the blank: he came to apologize but was instead ____.

feedback.correct_en: お礼を言われる ('to be thanked') is the ironic flip — he came to apologize but got thanked instead.
feedback.incorrect_en: お詫び (apology) is what HE was going to give, not receive. お世話 doesn't fit the 言う collocation here.

prompt.context_jp: 「おいおい… 急に___なよ それは何か調子狂うわ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「急に___なよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Etsuko has suddenly apologized; Kaizuka says: 'Don't ___ all of a sudden.'

feedback.correct_en: 謝んなよ (= 謝るなよ, casual) 'don't apologize' — she just said ごめんなさい, which threw him off.
feedback.incorrect_en: 怒んな would mean 'don't get angry,' but she wasn't angry; 笑わな doesn't match the context.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に謝るなよ、調子狂う。
contrast_examples.en: Don't suddenly apologize, it throws me off.

prompt.context_jp: 「___だなぁ ___ お前のやってることは 全部 ___だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___だなぁ お前のやってることは全部___だ」
prompt.prompt_en: Kaizuka dismisses her flyer plan: 'This is ___. Everything you're doing is ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 無駄 ('pointless/wasted effort') is the chapter's keyword — it echoes throughout the episode.
feedback.incorrect_en: 無理 means 'impossible/unreasonable' — close but not the theme. 無口 means 'taciturn,' unrelated.

prompt.context_jp: 「先日は本当に 大変___ことを言ってしまい すいませんでした！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「大変___ことを言ってしまい すいませんでした」
prompt.prompt_en: Formal apology to Tokiko: 'I said something extremely ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 失礼な ('rude/impolite') fits an apology — Etsuko admits she was rude the other day.
feedback.incorrect_en: 便利な ('convenient') and 大切な ('important') don't make sense in an apology for one's behavior.

contrast_examples.jp: 失礼なことを言ってしまった。

contrast_examples.en: I have an important thing to discuss.

prompt.context_jp: 「そうしないと みんなの親切や努力が ___になっちゃうじゃない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「みんなの親切や努力が ___になっちゃうじゃない」
prompt.prompt_en: Tokiko's line: 'otherwise everyone's kindness and effort would become ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 無駄になる ('to go to waste') — Tokiko now uses the very word she'd been mocking, in a sincere way.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気になる means 'to get better'; 迷惑になる means 'to become a nuisance' — neither fits.

contrast_examples.jp: 迷惑になるから静かに。
contrast_examples.en: Be quiet, it'll be a nuisance.

prompt.context_jp: 「お荷物になると ___ないんですが 登紀子さんのお好きな 浅草のお菓子です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お荷物になると ___ないんですが…」
prompt.prompt_en: Polite preface before handing over a gift.

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ない ('I'm terribly sorry') is a standard polite hedge before imposing on someone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕方ない means 'can't be helped'; 問題ない means 'no problem' — neither works as a humble preface.

contrast_examples.jp: お手数おかけして申し訳ないのですが…
contrast_examples.en: I'm sorry to trouble you, but…

prompt.context_jp: 「森尾ちゃんも お前の性格は よく分かってるだろうし そこまで ___必要もねぇんじゃねぇ…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「そこまで ___必要もねぇんじゃねぇ…」
prompt.prompt_en: 'You don't need to ___ that much.'

feedback.correct_en: 気にする ('to worry/mind') fits — he's telling her Morio knows her, so no need to fret.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気がする means 'to have a feeling that…' 気をつける means 'to be careful' — neither matches.

contrast_examples.en: Don't worry about it so much.

prompt.context_jp: 「せっかく あんなオシャレ ___くれたのに 本当 ごめんね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「せっかく あんなオシャレ ___くれたのに…」
prompt.prompt_en: 'You went to the trouble of dressing up for me, and I…'

feedback.correct_en: おしゃれしてきてくれた means 'you dressed up (and came) for me' — してきて captures both 'did' and 'came.'
feedback.incorrect_en: いって / みえて don't form the natural 'went to the trouble of dressing up and coming' idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: わざわざ来てくれてありがとう。
contrast_examples.en: Thanks for coming all this way.

prompt.context_jp: 「自分が ___からとか言って 財布開けたら 280円しかないって どういうことだ お前」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「自分が ___からとか言って…」
prompt.prompt_en: 'You said YOU would ___ (treat me)…'

feedback.correct_en: おごる means 'to treat (someone)' — she said she'd pay but only has 280 yen.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらう ('to receive') and かりる ('to borrow') don't fit someone offering to pay.

prompt.context_jp: Etsuko unexpectedly enters the lobby scene and stops.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as a scene-introducing narration of Etsuko entering?

choices.text: そこを通りかかった悦子が、ふいに柱の陰で足を止めた。
そこを通りかかった悦子は、ふいに柱の陰で足を止めた。

feedback.correct_en: The relative clause 通りかかった悦子 introduces her into the scene; が is natural for this event-report style.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose Etsuko is already the running topic, which doesn't match this scene transition.

contrast_examples.jp: 通りかかった男が声をかけた。
その男は何も言わなかった。

prompt.context_jp: Kaizuka downplays going to Asakusa to buy sweets for Tokiko.
prompt.prompt_en: Which humble phrasing sounds more natural in this business-polite context?

choices.text: 浅草なんてもうすぐそこですから、大した手間じゃないんですよ。
浅草なんてもうすぐそこだから、大変手間じゃないんですよ。

feedback.correct_en: 大した〜ない ('not much of…') is the set idiom for downplaying effort. ですから keeps the register polite.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大変手間じゃない mixes 大変 (very) with a negation that doesn't collocate; だから also drops politeness mid-sentence.

prompt.context_jp: Etsuko describes how she blurts things out.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the natural idiom for 'words rush out before I think'?

choices.text: 考える前に 口をついて出ちゃうんだよね
考える前に 口から走って出ちゃうんだよね

feedback.correct_en: 口をついて出る is the set phrase for words slipping out involuntarily.
feedback.incorrect_en: 口から走って出る isn't an established idiom and sounds literal/odd.

contrast_examples.jp: 本音が口をついて出た。

prompt.context_jp: Etsuko abruptly makes an excuse to flee the awkward moment with Yukito.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as a flustered excuse to leave?

choices.text: 私 会社 行かなきゃいけないから、ごめんね!
私は会社に行かなければいけませんので、申し訳ありません。

feedback.correct_en: The casual 行かなきゃ + ごめんね matches her panicked, personal tone with Yukito.
feedback.incorrect_en: The formal keigo version sounds like a business apology to a stranger — wrong register for a date-partner.

contrast_examples.jp: もう行かなきゃ、またね!

prompt.context_jp: Etsuko explains her stubborn proofreading principle.
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression naturally conveys 'I can't rest until I check'?

choices.text: 気になったことは 確認しないと気が済まないから
気になったことは 確認しないと気が終わらないから

feedback.correct_en: 気が済まない is the idiom for 'can't be satisfied / won't rest until…'
feedback.incorrect_en: 気が終わる isn't a real collocation — 終わる doesn't pair with 気 this way.

contrast_examples.jp: やらないと気が済まない。
contrast_examples.en: I can't rest until I do it.

contrast_examples.jp: 謝るまで気が済まなかった。
contrast_examples.en: I couldn't settle until I apologized.
